title: Self-calibrating thermal interferometry of vortex parity in a two-dimensional chiral superconductor
abstract: A chiral superconductor carries chiral Majorana modes along its boundary, and the integer that counts them fixes everything that follows, yet that integer has never been measured together with a local parity observable on one object. Proximitized one-dimensional wires read fermion parity rapidly but diagnose bulk topology through a separate protocol. Here we show that a reconfigurable domain wall between regions of opposite Chern number in an intrinsic two-dimensional chiral superconductor performs both functions. Opened to its contacts the wall is a ballistic channel whose quantized thermal conductance counts its Majorana modes; closed, the same wall is a Fabry--Pérot resonator whose spectrum shifts by half a level spacing when the parity of the enclosed vortices changes, giving a two-level heat conductance. We derive the exact transmission, the elastic heat full counting statistics, and a theorem showing that linear-response heat scattering of a fixed quadratic problem resolves vortex parity but not the fusion channel of well-separated cores. An outside vortex hybridized with the wall is an intrinsic false positive; temperature, geometry and a finite-bias mean--noise test separates it. Rhombohedral-graphene parameters place submicron loops in the resolved regime at millikelvin temperatures, where chiral-domain reconfiguration and noise thermometry are both established.
summary: This work demonstrates a method to measure both the bulk topological invariant and the local vortex parity in a chiral superconductor using a reconfigurable domain wall. By tuning the wall between open (measuring bulk conductance) and closed (measuring spectral shifts) configurations, the device performs two distinct topological diagnostics. This offers a powerful tool for characterizing Majorana physics in solid-state systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simultaneously measuring both the bulk topological invariant (Chern number) and a local parity observable (vortex parity) in a two-dimensional chiral superconductor.
main_result: A reconfigurable domain wall structure allows for this dual measurement: quantized thermal conductance probes the bulk invariant when open, while spectral shifts in a Fabry-Pérot resonator read out vortex parity when closed.
method: The authors use thermal interferometry, calculating quantized heat conductance and analyzing the shift in the single-particle energy spectrum based on the boundary conditions imposed by the enclosed vortex parity.
model_or_system: The physical system is an intrinsic two-dimensional chiral superconductor realized in rhombohedral graphene, featuring a tunable domain wall separating regions of opposite Chern numbers. The theoretical framework relies on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian and the bulk-boundary correspondence.
key_observables: Quantized thermal conductance, spectral shifts (half a level spacing), and the heat full counting statistics.
important_parameters: Millikelvin temperatures, submicron loop sizes, and the gap ratio ($\Delta_0$) are key experimental scales.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to treat the system using a quadratic scattering matrix and requires coherent propagation and weak inelastic equilibration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry, the single-particle spectrum for different boundary conditions (R/NS sectors), and the resulting transmission probability $T(\epsilon)$ which depends on the enclosed vortex parity.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the dual-functionality of the domain wall, deriving the transmission and thermal conductance formulas, and then analyzing the spectral signatures that distinguish bulk topology from local parity.
why_interesting: The technique provides a novel, highly sensitive, and non-destructive method to probe topological invariants and local quantum numbers simultaneously using thermal transport, which is relevant for understanding topological quantum computation platforms.

In experiment the vortex- entry fields need not be equally spaced; the signature is the conductance switch correlated with vortex parity.
